target_customer: Players who want instant play, and game studios paying for web porting and distribution on the platform
problem: Playing modern games requires large downloads, launchers and hardware. Wavedash runs games locally in the browser through WebAssembly and WebGPU so a link starts play in seconds.
business_model: game storefront with developer revenue share plus porting services for studios

founders.name: Kyler Blue
founders.background_notes: Per YC page: first employee and head of product at Tenor, which Google acquired.

founders.name: Matthew Portner
founders.background_notes: Per YC page; the YC page lists three founders although some press names two.

technical_complexity.rationale: Running high end engine builds in the browser with WebAssembly and WebGPU, handling shader stutter and memory, and building SDKs for many engines is hard for three people.

defensibility.rationale: Value depends on a catalog and audience that do not yet exist, and engines and browsers could support the same path; one outlet notes developers may hesitate to port to a store with no audience.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Wavedash through late 2025.

market_need_then: Browser capabilities (WebAssembly, WebGPU) had matured by 2025 and install friction hurts game discovery, but demand for high end games in tabs was unproven.

branding.domain_note: Press contact uses wavedash.gg; docs live on docs.wavedash.com. An older unrelated Wavedash Games studio also used the name.

identity.voice_and_tone: Click a link and start playing in seconds

branding.brand_signature: Click a link and play with no download
branding.community_and_virality: Launched on Product Hunt on 2025-12-16 with 111 upvotes per a listing; a gamedev news item reports a Defold Foundation partnership.

brand_strength.rationale: The name evokes a Smash Bros movement term familiar to gamers, but sources do not say that, and an older studio of the same name creates some confusion.

outcome_analysis: Wavedash joined YC in Spring 2025 and raised a $4.3M seed led by Floodgate with a public beta on 2025-12-15 and a launch title from indie developer Walaber. Founders have prior consumer and music startup exits. Whether developers port to a new storefront remains the open risk, and the company is still active with no exit.
notes: The seed is covered by GamesBeat, Mobidictum and a press release syndication. The company site wavedash.com could not be fetched because of a safety check rate limit. The brand strength rationale does not claim a name origin; none was found. No dated competitor sources near the Spring 2025 batch were found, so the list is empty. A claimed 90 percent developer revenue share came from one aggregator and is not recorded.
